text.p: Mexican retail firm Cifra SA is expected to report lackluster earnings for 1996 due to a lingering slump in consumer demand, analysts said.
A survey of four analysts showed average predicted net earnings of 51 centavos per share, compared with 53 centavos in 1995.
The analysts forecasted average net consolidated earnings of 1.580 billion pesos, or 20.2 percent less than the 1.9797 billion posted in 1995.
"Cifra's earnings may come in a little lower than expected, not because of Cifra in particular, but the sector as a whole," said Roberto Calderon, an analyst with Santander Investment.

"Almost all retail firms bet on December and greater recovery in the economy. Nonetheless, consumers are very cautious because it is so hard to wipe clean the effects of 1994," he said, referring to the 1994-1995 peso crisis.

"Cifra's problem is the location of its stores, around 65 percent of which are in the Mexico City area, where consumption has recovered more slowly than in the (industrialized) north," said Humberto Garcia, an analyst with Invex brokerage in Mexico City.
Sales volumes were forecast at 23.675 billion pesos for 1996, down from the 25.530 billion chalked up in 1995.
Nonetheless, other analysts said that lower volumes could be offset by a higher operating margin, optimizing cost-control and a less aggressive pricing policy during the fourth quarter.

"We see Cifra's operating earnings as good. There has been a recovery in subsidiaries that were having problems, like VIPs (restaurants) and Suburbia (department stores). Margins will definitely be better," said an analyst who wished to remain anonymous.
